title: Music arranger
evidenceStatus: Five completed authored eight-note motifs; three provider-429 failures; no listening evaluation.
summary: All five completed motifs rise or repeat until a final tonic reset; four are literal scale walks. Playback overrides 31 of 40 note durations and all three sine-voice choices, while the default ABAB transposition creates 20 of 160 notes outside the recorded scale and 80 piano-roll pitch mismatches. Build a shared score and contextual phrase candidates before judging Jev's musical quality.
strengths: Uses Tone's scheduled audio time after user-initiated audio startup.
Four separately audible and muteable parts make the arrangement inspectable.
Preserves full typed decisions and distributions and explicitly credits procedural arrangement code.
Existing Tone.js and @tonejs/midi dependencies can support a much richer implementation.

findings.title: Ordinal note questions collapse to ascending scale walks
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:374; results/music.jsonl:2; probes/music.probe.json: 4/5 literal scale walks, 29 upward intervals, 1 repeat, 5 final downward resets, no earlier descent.
findings.impact: Independent questions see no phrase history and ordinal positions echo degree names, preventing meaningful musical-context decisions. The suspected naming cause still needs an ablation.
findings.fix: Generate coherent two-bar phrase candidates with varied contours, rhythm and rests, then have Jev choose against the brief, harmony and previous phrase. Test neutral identifiers and relative-motion questions separately.

findings.title: Audio discards most recorded rhythm and timbre decisions
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/creative.tsx:478, :511, :545; 31/40 durations differ from fixed eighth-note playback; 3/5 recorded voices are sine but playback always uses triangle.
findings.impact: The audible result does not represent the model choices being presented. Original phrase lengths of 16, 7.5, 9, 4 and 8 beats all become four beats.
findings.fix: Compile explicit beat-offset, duration, pitch, velocity, instrument and rest events. Enforce phrase length in candidates and use the score for playback and export.

findings.title: Form and harmony ignore the chosen key and phrase
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/creative.tsx:499, :515; default ABAB transposes by two semitones over fixed C/F/G/C roots; 20/160 melody events leave the recorded scale.
findings.impact: Chromatic notes and major chords over minor motifs arise without a musical decision, and B sections are fixed transpositions rather than phrase development.
findings.fix: Use tonic/mode-aware progressions, explicit permitted chromaticism, voice-leading code and phrase transformations such as inversion, rhythmic variation and instrument exchange.

findings.title: Visual and exported scores disagree with playback
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/creative.tsx:569, :734, :747, :756; default ABAB has 80/160 displayed pitch mismatches; MIDI and audio use different durations.
findings.impact: Visitors cannot inspect or edit what they hear, and exported files change articulation and timing.
findings.fix: Use one event list for piano roll, playback, MIDI and JSON; add pitch up/down, rest, duration, undo and phrase-lock controls; verify a one-tick MIDI round trip.

findings.title: Coverage and quality evaluation are incomplete
findings.evidence: results/music.jsonl:1, :6, :7, :8; human_preference is null; scripts/recover.ts:13 excludes music; package.json:10 has no music tests.
findings.impact: Five examples cannot establish coherence or superiority to procedural arrangement, and provider overload leaves three briefs unrepresented.
findings.fix: Recover only the three failed requests, preserve every completed choice, publish eight-case coverage and compare against rule and random baselines with independent blind listening.

findings.title: Pending audio startup can survive stop or navigation
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/creative.tsx:470, :476, :547, :616; async startup completes before engine.current and playing are set. Static risk, not browser-reproduced.
findings.impact: Rapid actions can leave stale audio startup or use stale motif state, undermining the interactive demo.
findings.fix: Add explicit playback states, generation tokens after awaits, ownership-aware disposal and score-version checks for late arrangement responses.

simulation.title: Score a tiny film
simulation.description: An eight-bar film scene drives a six-track score. Visitors audition alternatives for each two-bar scene, request a falling answer or more tension, lock phrases, edit notes and hear accepted changes at bar boundaries.
simulation.jevsRole: Choose semantic global settings and one coherent phrase candidate at a time, conditioned on scene direction, actual candidate events, harmony and prior selected phrases.
simulation.codeRole: Generate valid candidates; enforce meter, register, permitted harmony and locks; compute voice leading; schedule audio and synchronized animation; render and export one canonical score.
acceptanceCriteria: Audio, piano roll and MIDI share pitches, onset times and durations within one MIDI tick.
Six contour families, rests and syncopation are available, selectable and audible.
Eight bars span 32 beats at 4/4; each phrase spans eight beats including rests.
Chord labels match actual notes and inversions; intentional chromaticism is explicit.
Changes apply on bar boundaries without a transport restart or network call in the scheduler.
Stop and navigation cancel pending startup and all owned audio work.
Overload leaves the current score playing and never relabels a procedural fallback as Jev.
Keyboard editing works in both pitch directions and supports rests, mutes, undo and phrase locks.
One complete recorded session can be replayed without an API key, with candidates and decision provenance.

evaluation.design: Recover the three original transient failures. Freeze 48 authored briefs spanning six contours, four emotional trajectories and two phrase contexts; use four candidate-generation seeds for 192 new-system cases. Evaluate every score mechanically and compare methods with blind scene-fit judgments. New Jev arrangements require 960 logical calls, the original formulation 48, and two option-order checks for 48 final-phrase prompts 96, totaling 1,104 study calls plus three recoveries and retries. For listening, use 96 held-out A/B comparisons with five ratings each, randomized order, ties allowed and confidence intervals clustered by brief. No outcomes from this proposed study exist yet.
baselines: Original independent-note question formulation through the corrected shared renderer
Declared rule-based arranger over the same candidate pool
Uniform random selection over the same valid candidate pool
metrics: Full event parity across audio, piano roll and MIDI
Meter, register and user-lock constraint satisfaction
Exact contour, rhythm and instrumentation compliance where objectively specified
Blind scene-fit preference with ties worth half and 95% intervals clustered by brief; proposed success requires lower bound above 50%
Listener-rated phrase shape and distracting transitions
Unique interval/rhythm patterns, interval directions and terminal leaps as diagnostics
Edit latency, bar-boundary adoption, stale-response rejection, audio discontinuities and separate provider availability

coverage.current: 5 completed motifs from 8 authored briefs, 40 notes and 95 typed answers; 3 provider HTTP 429 failures.
coverage.full: All 8 original briefs, then a proposed 48-brief by 4-seed candidate study. There is no external music benchmark or official split in the current experiment.
coverage.feasibility: Completing the original set needs 3 logical calls with 19 questions each. The richer automated study needs 1,104 logical calls and the independent listening study needs 480 human judgments. Candidate generation, a shared score and renderer parity must be implemented first.

libraries.name: Tone.js
libraries.use: Keep the existing scheduler and synths; schedule score events, named instrument banks, buses and optional licensed samples while Jev selects semantic arrangement changes.

libraries.name: Tonal
libraries.use: Use notes, keys, chord progressions, voicings and voice-leading modules to generate valid contextual candidates that Jev can rank by scene fit.

libraries.name: @tonejs/midi
libraries.use: Export and import MIDI from the shared event score, round-trip pitches and timings, and let Jev arrange a visitor's motif.

nextSteps.action: Build the canonical score and parity across renderer, piano roll and MIDI; preserve predicted durations and timbres.
Add contextual phrase candidates, key-aware harmony, voice leading and an editable six-track arrangement.
Add playback generation guards, score-version checks and bar-quantized editing.
Recover only the three failed authored requests and publish coverage separately from quality.
Run the frozen 48-brief evaluation and blind listening before claiming quality improvements.
Reuse the conductor for context-sensitive Snake or Orbital rescue music with a fixed soundtrack-table baseline.
